facts.text: Yanceyville was founded in 1791 as Caswell Court House and renamed in 1833 to honor U.S. Representative Bartlett Yancey.
The town’s courthouse, built between 1858 and 1861 with enslaved labor, still stands as a National Register landmark in Yanceyville’s historic core.
Caswell County, where Yanceyville sits, was carved out of Orange County in 1777 to bring government services closer to residents.
Yanceyville’s economy once thrived on bright leaf tobacco, but the town’s lack of a railroad or major waterway left it reliant on agriculture after the Civil War.
The Yanceyville Rotary Club, founded in 1937, launched projects that helped spur local economic growth and community development.
In the mid‑2020s, the state’s Completing Access to Broadband program began expanding high‑speed internet to Yanceyville, aiming to modernize the town’s connectivity.
